Level of obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be prohibited'); describes a prohibition
Position: not stated
Quote: novel and powerful tools for manipulative, exploitative and social control practices. Such practices are particularly harmful and abusive and should be prohibited
Note: Decides that certain tools may not be used at all. Recital (29) covers AI that materially distorts behaviour through subliminal, manipulative or deceptive techniques, or exploits vulnerabilities (age, disability, social or economic situation), causing significant harm; 'it is not necessary for the provider or the deployer to have the intention to cause significant harm'. Lawful medical practice is not affected. Nearest named actors: providers and deployers (placing on the market, putting into service or use). Operative rule appears to be Art. 5 [inference; not in this part].

Level of obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes a Member State option
Position: public authority: Member State
Quote: Member States remain free under this Regulation not to provide for such a possibility at all or to only provide for such a possibility in respect of some of the objectives
Note: Real-time remote biometric identification for law enforcement is possible only where and in so far as the Member State 'has decided to expressly provide for the possibility to authorise such use in its detailed rules of national law'. Also coded Coordination/Design (notification of national rules).

Level of obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital, 'should be prohibited'); describes a prohibition
Position: not stated
Quote: Natural persons should never be judged on AI-predicted behaviour based solely on their profiling, personality traits or characteristics
Note: Prohibits individual crime-risk assessments based solely on profiling or personality traits 'without a reasonable suspicion ... based on objective verifiable facts and without human assessment thereof'. Not covered: risk analytics not based on profiling individuals, e.g. tools 'to predict the likelihood of the localisation of narcotics or illicit goods by customs authorities'. Nearest named actors: law enforcement and customs authorities.

Level of obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes a derogation from high-risk classification
Holder: a provider who considers that an AI system is not high-risk
Position: public authority or private company (provider)
Quote: an AI system that does not materially influence the outcome of decision-making should be understood to be an AI system that does not have an impact on the substance, and thereby the outcome, of decision-making
Note: The provider decides whether an annex-listed system falls under the derogation. Four conditions: (1) narrow procedural task, e.g. 'an AI system that classifies incoming documents into categories' or detects duplicates among applications; (2) improves the result of a completed human activity, e.g. improving language in drafted documents; (3) detects decision-making patterns or deviations, e.g. checking a teacher's grading ex post; (4) preparatory task, e.g. file handling, indexing, searching, translation. Systems that imply profiling are always high-risk. Many of the examples are public-administration tasks. Cross-ref Delivery/Design and Accountability/Design (Recital 53).

Level of obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes high-risk classification set by the Regulation
Position: not stated
Quote: for monitoring and detecting prohibited behaviour of students during tests should be classified as high-risk AI systems
Note: Education and vocational training: also determining access or admission, assigning persons to institutions or programmes, evaluating learning outcomes, and assessing the appropriate level of education. Nearest named actors: providers and deployers (including public education bodies [inference]).

Level of obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes high-risk classification set by the Regulation
Position: not stated
Quote: for monitoring or evaluation of persons in work-related contractual relationships, should also be classified as high-risk
Note: Employment and workers management: also recruitment and selection, decisions on terms, promotion and termination, and task allocation based on behaviour or traits. Applies to public bodies as employers [inference]. Nearest named actors: providers and deployers.

Level of obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes an exclusion from high-risk classification
Position: not stated
Quote: for administrative proceedings by tax and customs authorities as well as by financial intelligence units carrying out administrative tasks analysing information pursuant to Union anti-money laundering law should not be classified as high-risk
Note: Exclusion for public bodies: tax and customs administrative proceedings and FIU administrative analysis are not law-enforcement high-risk uses. Nearest named actors: tax and customs authorities, financial intelligence units.

Position: not stated
Quote: the difficulty in obtaining meaningful information on the functioning of those systems and the resulting difficulty in challenging their results in court
Note: States that the impact of AI tools on suspects' defence rights 'should not be ignored', especially the difficulty of challenging results in court; no mechanism is set out here. Also: AI use by law enforcement 'should not become a factor of inequality, or exclusion'. Nearest named actors: law enforcement and other relevant authorities. To whom: courts (implied [inference]); consequence: not stated.

Level of obligation: non-binding interpretation (recital); describes high-risk classification set by the Regulation
Position: not stated
Quote: AI systems intended to be used to influence the outcome of an election or referendum or the voting behaviour of natural persons in the exercise of their vote in elections or referenda should be classified as high-risk AI systems
Note: Excludes tools whose output persons are not directly exposed to (e.g. campaign logistics). Relevance to public-sector tools is indirect [inference]. Nearest named actors: providers and deployers.

Position: not stated
Quote: High-risk AI systems should be designed in a manner to enable deployers to understand how the AI system works, evaluate its functionality, and comprehend its strengths and limitations.
Note: Transparency 'should be required for high-risk AI systems before they are placed on the market or put it into service'. Nearest named actor: provider. Serves deployers' evaluation and correct use.

Holder: authorised representative (a person established in the Union)
Position: outside the state: private companies [inference]
Quote: a person established in the Union can provide authorities with all the necessary information on the compliance of an AI system.
Note: Contact point between non-EU providers and authorities. Cross-ref Accountability/Design (Recital 82).

Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: the standardisation requests should be issued by the Commission without undue delay. When preparing the standardisation request, the Commission should consult the advisory forum and the Board in order to collect relevant expertise.
Note: Standard-setting: harmonised standards are 'a means for providers to demonstrate conformity'. A balanced representation of interests in standard development 'should therefore be encouraged'. Consulting the advisory forum and the Board is also a Coordination link.

Holder: law enforcement authorities or civil protection authorities
Position: public authority: member-state authority
Quote: law enforcement authorities or civil protection authorities may put a specific high-risk AI system into service without the authorisation of the market surveillance authority, provided that such authorisation is requested during or after the use without undue delay.
Note: Answers to: the market surveillance authority, after the fact. Consequence if authorisation refused: not stated here. Cross-ref Decision-making/Design (same quote).

Position: not stated
Quote: The supervision of the AI systems in the AI regulatory sandbox should therefore cover their development, training, testing and validation before the systems are placed on the market or put into service
Note: Regulatory oversight of sandbox participants, including 'the notion and occurrence of substantial modification that may require a new conformity assessment procedure'. Nearest named actors: national competent authorities. Cross-ref Decision-making/Design (suspension, Recital 139).

Holder: Each market surveillance authority for high-risk AI systems in the area of biometrics
Position: public authority: member-state market surveillance authority
Quote: the power to obtain access to all personal data that are being processed and to all information necessary for the performance of its tasks
Note: Access to data and information provided to MSAs for investigation and enforcement. Limits on access to sensitive operational data are without prejudice to Directive (EU) 2016/680 powers. Also coded Decision-making/Design.

Position: public authority: EU institution (AI Office is a Commission function, Art. 3(47))
Quote: The AI Office should provide coordination support for joint investigations.
Note: Support provided for the joint investigations in the same recital (Coordination/Design).

Position: public authority: EU advisory panel; EU institution
Quote: there should be a mechanism whereby the scientific panel can request the Commission to require documentation or information from a provider
Note: Information resource for the panel's alert role; serves oversight of GPAI model providers.

Position: public authority: EU institution (AI Office is a Commission function, Art. 3(47))
Quote: including by requesting documentation and information, by conducting evaluations, as well as by requesting measures from providers of general-purpose AI models
Note: Recital: 'The AI Office should be able to investigate possible infringements in accordance with the powers provided for in this Regulation'. GPAI model providers answer to the AI Office. Safeguard: providers 'should have the procedural rights provided for in Article 18 of Regulation (EU) 2019/1020'. Also coded Decision-making/Design and Accountability/Resources.

Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: It is of particular importance that the Commission carry out appropriate consultations during its preparatory work, including at expert level
Note: Per Interinstitutional Agreement on Better Law-Making (13 April 2016); Parliament and Council receive all documents with Member States' experts and access Commission expert group meetings.

Position: public authority: EU legislature [inference]
Quote: providers placing on the market or putting into service AI systems or placing on the market general-purpose AI models in the Union, irrespective of whether those providers are established or located within the Union or in a third country
Note: Scope set by the Regulation itself. Brings non-EU model and system providers into scope. Art. 2(1)(c): also third-country providers and deployers where output is used in the Union.

Position: public authority: EU legislature [inference]
Quote: applies neither to public authorities in a third country nor to international organisations falling within the scope of this Regulation pursuant to paragraph 1, where those authorities or organisations use AI systems in the framework of international cooperation
Note: Condition: international cooperation or agreements for law enforcement and judicial cooperation with the Union or Member States, with adequate safeguards for fundamental rights.

Position: mixed: private companies or public authorities
Quote: ‘provider’ means a natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body that develops an AI system or a general-purpose AI model or that has an AI system or a general-purpose AI model developed
Note: Definition continues: 'and places it on the market or puts the AI system into service under its own name or trademark'. [inference] A public authority that develops or commissions a system and puts it into service under its own name (incl. own use, Art. 3(11)) holds provider obligations.

Position: mixed: public authorities or private bodies
Quote: ‘deployer’ means a natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body using an AI system under its authority except where the AI system is used in the course of a personal non-professional activity
Note: Makes public authorities that use AI 'deployers', holding deployer obligations (e.g. Arts 4, 26, 27, 49(3), 50).

If not met: Art. 99(3) (outside this part): administrative fines up to EUR 35 000 000 or 7% of worldwide turnover; Union bodies up to EUR 1 500 000 (Art. 100(2)); fines on national public authorities only as each Member State lays down (Art. 99(8)).
Position: mixed (nearest actors: providers and deployers, incl. public authorities)
Quote: The following AI practices shall be prohibited:
Note: Bars use outright for anyone placing on the market, putting into service or using. Listed: (a) subliminal/manipulative techniques causing significant harm; (b) exploiting vulnerabilities (age, disability, social or economic situation); (c) social scoring; (d) criminal-offence risk prediction based solely on profiling; (e) untargeted scraping for facial recognition databases; (f) emotion inference in workplace and education (except medical/safety); (g) biometric categorisation inferring race, political opinions, trade union membership, religion, sex life or orientation; (h) real-time remote biometric identification in public spaces for law enforcement save listed objectives. (c), (d), (h) coded separately. Applies from 2 February 2025 (Recital 179).

If not met: use is not to be authorised ('shall be authorised only if')
Position: public authority: member-state law enforcement
Quote: has registered the system in the EU database according to Article 49. However, in duly justified cases of urgency, the use of such systems may be commenced without the registration in the EU database
Note: In urgency, registration must be 'completed without undue delay'. Registration for law enforcement is in a non-public section (Art. 49(4)).

Level of obligation: statutory duty (for Member States that opt in)
Position: public authority: member-state government
Quote: Member States concerned shall lay down in their national law the necessary detailed rules for the request, issuance and exercise of, as well as supervision and reporting relating to, the authorisations referred to in paragraph 3
Note: Rules must also specify the objectives and criminal offences for which competent authorities may be authorised. Also coded Coordination/Design (notify rules to Commission).

If not met: Not stated here. Providers must ensure compliance with Section 2 (Art. 16(a)); breach of Art. 16 attracts fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part); Union bodies up to EUR 750 000 (Art. 100(3)).
Position: mixed (nearest actor: provider)
Quote: A risk management system shall be established, implemented, documented and maintained in relation to high-risk AI systems.
Note: Passive; nearest named actor: providers (Art. 9(9), 16(a)). Art. 9(2): 'a continuous iterative process planned and run throughout the entire lifecycle', with 'regular systematic review and updating'. Steps: identify/analyse known and foreseeable risks to health, safety, fundamental rights; estimate/evaluate under intended use and foreseeable misuse; evaluate risks from post-market monitoring data (Art. 72); adopt targeted measures. Trigger: ongoing.

If not met: Not stated here; 'technical documentation is not available' is a formal non-compliance: MSA requires the provider to end it, and if it persists restricts, prohibits, recalls or withdraws the system (Art. 83, outside this part).
Position: mixed (nearest actor: provider)
Quote: to provide national competent authorities and notified bodies with the necessary information in a clear and comprehensive form to assess the compliance of the AI system with those requirements
Note: The documentation lets the provider answer to NCAs and notified bodies. Also coded Delivery/Design.

If not met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3%; incorrect information in reply: up to EUR 7 500 000 or 1% (Art. 99(5)).
Position: mixed: private companies or public authorities (Art. 3(3))
Quote: upon a reasoned request of a national competent authority, demonstrate the conformity of the high-risk AI system with the requirements set out in Section 2
Note: Provider answers to NCAs. See Art. 21.

If not met: Not stated here. Art. 16(j) breach: Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part).
Position: mixed: private companies or public authorities (Art. 3(3))
Quote: inform the market surveillance authorities competent for the high-risk AI system concerned and, where applicable, the notified body that issued a certificate for that high-risk AI system
Note: Report covers 'the nature of the non-compliance and of any relevant corrective action taken'. Answers to MSAs and notified body; consequence not stated here.

If not met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(b) (outside this part): fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3%.
Position: outside the state: private companies (EU-established representative)
Quote: provide a competent authority, upon a reasoned request, with all the information and documentation, including that referred to in point (b) of this subparagraph, necessary to demonstrate the conformity of a high-risk AI system
Note: (b) keep provider contact details, EU declaration, technical documentation and certificate for 10 years; (c) incl. log access; (d) cooperate to reduce and mitigate risks; (e) registration under Art. 49(1) or check registration data. Provides copy of mandate to MSAs on request.

If not met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(b) (outside this part).
Position: outside the state: private companies (EU-established representative)
Quote: it shall immediately inform the relevant market surveillance authority, as well as, where applicable, the relevant notified body, about the termination of the mandate and the reasons therefor
Note: Trigger: representative 'shall terminate the mandate if it considers or has reason to consider the provider to be acting contrary to its obligations'. Reports the provider to the MSA.

If not met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(d) (outside this part).
Position: outside the state: private companies
Quote: shall take the corrective actions necessary to bring that system into conformity with those requirements, to withdraw it or recall it, or shall ensure that the provider, the importer or any relevant operator, as appropriate, takes those corrective actions
Note: For systems already made available. Where risk under Art. 79(1): immediately inform provider or importer and competent authorities with details of non-compliance and corrective actions (accountability element).

Level of obligation: statutory duty (resource the initial provider must give the new provider)
Position: mixed: private companies or public authorities
Quote: make available the necessary information and provide the reasonably expected technical access and other assistance that are required for the fulfilment of the obligations set out in this Regulation
Note: Information and technical access for the new provider (e.g. a deployer that became provider under 25(1)), 'in particular regarding the compliance with the conformity assessment'. Also coded Coordination/Design.

Holder: The provider of a high-risk AI system and the third party that supplies an AI system, tools, services, components, or processes
Position: mixed: providers (public or private); suppliers outside the state: private companies
Quote: The provider of a high-risk AI system and the third party that supplies an AI system, tools, services, components, or processes that are used or integrated in a high-risk AI system shall, by written agreement, specify the necessary information
Note: Supplier contracts: specify information, capabilities, technical access and assistance 'based on the generally acknowledged state of the art' so the provider can comply. Not for free and open-source tools other than general-purpose AI models.

If not met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(f) (outside this part).
Position: mixed: private companies or public authorities (Art. 3(3))
Quote: Activities may be subcontracted or carried out by a subsidiary only with the agreement of the provider.
Note: The assessed provider holds a veto over subcontracting of its assessment.

If not met: Not stated here. Art. 99(4)(f) (outside this part).
Position: outside the state: third-party conformity assessment bodies
Quote: Notified bodies shall make a list of their subsidiaries publicly available.
Note: Publication.

Position: public authority: member-state authority
Quote: The notifying authority shall notify the Commission and the other Member States of any relevant changes to the notification of a notified body via the electronic notification tool referred to in Article 30(2).
Note: Extensions of scope follow Arts 29-30 procedures (36(2)).

Position: public authority: member-state authority
Quote: it shall restrict, suspend or withdraw the designation as appropriate, depending on the seriousness of the failure to meet those requirements or fulfil those obligations
Note: Trigger: sufficient reason to consider the notified body no longer meets Art. 31 or fails its obligations; investigate 'with the utmost diligence', hear the body, inform Commission and Member States. Notified bodies answer to the notifying authority; consequence: loss of designation. 36(5): notified body informs providers within 10 days; 36(6): files kept and made available to other authorities.

Holder: the national competent authority of the Member State in which the provider of the system covered by the certificate has its place of business
Position: public authority: member-state authority
Quote: may extend the provisional validity of the certificates for additional periods of three months, which shall not exceed 12 months in total
Note: After withdrawal of designation, certificates remain valid nine months if the NCA confirms no risk and another notified body assumes responsibility and completes assessment within 12 months. 36(8): rules for suspension or restriction (notifying authority confirms no risk, or provider confirms another notified body within three months).

Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: The Commission shall provide for the exchange of knowledge and best practices between notifying authorities.
Note: Network among notifying authorities.

Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: When drafting the common specifications, the Commission shall consult the advisory forum referred to in Article 67.
Note: 41(2): Commission informs the committee under Art. 22 of Regulation (EU) No 1025/2012 before drafting.

Holder: providers of high-risk AI systems or general-purpose AI models
Position: mixed: private companies or public authorities (Art. 3(3))
Quote: they shall duly justify that they have adopted technical solutions that meet the requirements referred to in Section 2 of this Chapter
Note: Applies where they do not comply with common specifications; solutions must reach 'a level at least equivalent'. To whom the justification is given: not stated.

Level of obligation: mandatory approval gate (conformity assessment before placing on market, Art. 16(f))
If not met: Not stated here. Art. 16(f) breach: fines up to EUR 15 000 000 or 3% (Art. 99(4)(a), outside this part); national public authorities as each Member State lays down (Art. 99(8)).
Position: mixed: private companies or public authorities (Art. 3(3))
Quote: In demonstrating the compliance of a high-risk AI system with the requirements set out in Section 2, the provider shall follow the conformity assessment procedure set out in Annex VII where:
Note: Applies to Annex III point 1 (biometrics). If harmonised standards or common specifications were applied, the provider may opt for internal control (Annex VI) or notified-body assessment (Annex VII); Annex VII required where standards/specifications are absent, not applied, partly applied or restricted. Also coded Decision-making/Design and Delivery/Design (MSA as notified body).

Position: mixed: private companies or public authorities (Art. 3(3))
Quote: For the purposes of the conformity assessment procedure referred to in Annex VII, the provider may choose any of the notified bodies.
Note: The provider chooses its checker, except for systems intended for law enforcement, immigration, asylum authorities or EU bodies (MSA acts as notified body).

If not met: Not stated here. Art. 16(f) breach: Art. 99(4)(a) (outside this part).
Position: mixed (nearest actor: provider, incl. a deployer that becomes provider under Art. 25(1)(b))
Quote: shall undergo a new conformity assessment procedure in the event of a substantial modification, regardless of whether the modified system is intended to be further distributed or continues to be used by the current deployer
Note: Trigger: substantial modification (Art. 3(23)), even if the system stays with the current deployer. Pre-determined changes for continuously learning systems, documented in Annex IV point 2(f), are not substantial modifications.

If not met: Not stated here. Notified-body obligations under Art. 31, 33, 34 are fined under Art. 99(4)(f); Art. 45 not listed there (outside this part).
Position: outside the state: third-party conformity assessment bodies
Quote: Notified bodies shall inform the notifying authority of the following:
Note: Items: certificates and QMS approvals issued; refusals, restrictions, suspensions, withdrawals; circumstances affecting notification; MSA requests for information; on request, activities incl. cross-border and subcontracting.

Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 97 in order to amend Annex V by updating the content of the EU declaration of conformity
Note: Sets what the sign-off must contain.

Position: mixed (nearest actors: providers and deployers)
Quote: High-risk AI systems referred to in point 2 of Annex III shall be registered at national level.
Note: Point 2 of Annex III (content outside this part) is excluded from EU-database registration in 49(1) and 49(3); who registers and where nationally: not stated.

Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: based on a decision of the Commission, ex officio or following a qualified alert from the scientific panel, it has capabilities or an impact equivalent to those set out in point (a)
Note: Classification as GPAI model with systemic risk triggers Art. 55 duties. 51(1)(a): high impact capabilities evaluated by technical tools, indicators and benchmarks; (b) having regard to Annex XIII criteria.

Holder: the Commission (on reasoned request of the designated provider)
Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: the Commission shall take the request into account and may decide to reassess whether the general-purpose AI model can still be considered to present systemic risks
Note: Challenge route for providers: request must contain 'objective, detailed and new reasons'; earliest six months after designation and after any decision maintaining it.

Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: The Commission is empowered to adopt delegated acts in accordance with Article 97(2) to amend Annexes XI and XII in light of evolving technological developments.
Note: 53(5): delegated acts to detail measurement and calculation methodologies for comparable, verifiable documentation (Annex XI points 2(d), (e)).

Position: outside the state: private companies (EU-established representative)
Quote: verify that the technical documentation specified in Annex XI has been drawn up and all obligations referred to in Article 53 and, where applicable, Article 55 have been fulfilled by the provider
Note: Check on the model provider; trigger not stated.

Position: outside the state: private companies (EU-established representative)
Quote: In such a case, it shall also immediately inform the AI Office about the termination of the mandate and the reasons therefor.
Note: Trigger: representative 'shall terminate the mandate if it considers or has reason to consider the provider to be acting contrary to its obligations'. Reports the model provider to the AI Office.

If not met: Not stated here. Fines under Art. 101 (outside this part; see Recital 169).
Holder: Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risks
Position: outside the state: private companies (model providers) [inference: typically]
Quote: Providers of general-purpose AI models with systemic risks who do not adhere to an approved code of practice or do not comply with a European harmonised standard shall demonstrate alternative adequate means of compliance for assessment by the Commission.
Note: Codes of practice may be relied on until a harmonised standard is published. 55(3): confidentiality (Art. 78).

Holder: The AI Office and the Board
Position: public authority: EU institution; EU body
Quote: The AI Office and the Board shall aim to ensure that the codes of practice cover at least the obligations provided for in Articles 53 and 55
Note: Issues: keeping documentation up to date, detail of training-content summary, identification of systemic risks, risk assessment and management measures. 56(4): codes set objectives, commitments and KPIs and account for interests of affected persons.

Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: or if the AI Office deems it is not adequate following its assessment under paragraph 6 of this Article, the Commission may provide, by means of implementing acts, common rules
Note: Codes 'shall be ready at the latest by 2 May 2025'; fallback also if a code cannot be finalised by 2 August 2025.

Position: public authority: EU institution; EU body
Quote: the Commission and the Board shall be authorised to access the exit reports and shall take them into account, as appropriate, when exercising their tasks under this Regulation
Note: Subject to Art. 78 confidentiality and the provider's agreement.

Position: public authority: member-state competent authorities (nearest actors)
Quote: The establishment of AI regulatory sandboxes shall aim to contribute to the following objectives:
Note: Passive; nearest actors: Member States and competent authorities establishing sandboxes. Objectives: legal certainty; sharing best practices; innovation and an AI ecosystem; evidence-based regulatory learning; market access, esp. for SMEs. Points (b)-(e) fall on p. 89 (after line 4270) but belong to this passage.

Position: public authority: Member State authority
Quote: and shall inform the AI Office of such decision.
Note: The decision is a suspension of testing or of sandbox participation. Also coded Decision-making/Design.

If not met: [inference] the exemption from administrative fines no longer applies; fines under Art. 99 may then be imposed
Holder: Prospective providers participating in the AI regulatory sandbox
Position: outside the state: private companies (may also be public authorities)
Quote: provided that the prospective providers observe the specific plan and the terms and conditions for their participation and follow in good faith the guidance given by the national competent authority, no administrative fines shall be imposed
Note: Answer to: the national competent authority. The exemption extends to other Union and national law where other competent authorities were actively involved and gave guidance. Also coded Accountability/Design (liability).

Position: public authority: Member State authority
Quote: The AI regulatory sandboxes shall be designed and implemented in such a way that, where relevant, they facilitate cross-border cooperation between national competent authorities.
Note: Passive. Nearest named actors: national competent authorities that establish sandboxes.

Position: public authority: EU institution
Quote: The Commission shall proactively coordinate with national competent authorities, where relevant.
Note: Also coded Coordination/Resources (single interface).

Holder: Providers and prospective providers (applying with deployers and other third parties)
Position: outside the state: private companies; deployers may be public bodies
Quote: providers and prospective providers may also submit applications in partnerships with deployers and other relevant third parties
Note: [inference] Allows a public-sector deployer to enter a sandbox jointly with its supplier. Same point also requires broad and equal access.

Position: not stated
Quote: that they facilitate providers and prospective providers, by means of the learning outcomes of the AI regulatory sandboxes, in complying with conformity assessment obligations under this Regulation
Note: Serves conformity assessment and voluntary codes of conduct (Art. 95). Nearest named actors: national competent authorities operating sandboxes; the Commission sets the arrangements by implementing act.

Level of obligation: statutory duty (content the implementing acts 'shall ensure')
Position: not stated
Quote: AI regulatory sandboxes facilitate the involvement of other relevant actors within the AI ecosystem, such as notified bodies and standardisation organisations
Note: List continues: SMEs, enterprises, innovators, testing and experimentation facilities, research labs, European Digital Innovation Hubs, centres of excellence, individual researchers, 'in order to allow and facilitate cooperation with the public and private sectors'. Nearest named actor: national competent authorities.

Level of obligation: statutory duty (content the implementing acts 'shall ensure')
Position: not stated
Quote: participation in an AI regulatory sandbox established by a Member State, or by the European Data Protection Supervisor is mutually and uniformly recognised and carries the same legal effects across the Union
Note: Mutual recognition across Member States. The EDPS can run a sandbox [inference: for Union institutions, bodies, offices and agencies]. Also requires simple, intelligible procedures streamlined across the Union.

Position: public authority: Member State authority
Quote: participation in the AI regulatory sandbox is limited to a period that is appropriate to the complexity and scale of the project and that may be extended by the national competent authority
Note: Duration decision held by the national competent authority.

Position: public authority: Member State authority
Quote: Where appropriate, they shall cooperate with other national competent authorities with a view to ensuring consistent practices across the Union.
Note: Also coded Decision-making/Design.

If not met: [inference] the further processing of personal data is not permitted under this Article ('may be processed solely ... when all of the following conditions are met')
Position: public authority or outside the state (developer may be a public authority or another natural or legal person)
Quote: AI systems shall be developed for safeguarding substantial public interest by a public authority or another natural or legal person
Note: Gate for further processing, in the sandbox, of personal data lawfully collected for other purposes, solely for developing, training and testing. Areas include '(v) efficiency and quality of public administration and public services', public safety and health, environment, energy, transport and critical infrastructure. Conditions are cumulative ((a)-(j)). Nearest named actors: the public authority or other person developing the system; [inference] applied by the supervising competent authority.

If not met: [inference] the further processing is not permitted
Position: public authority or outside the state
Quote: any personal data to be processed in the context of the sandbox are in a functionally separate, isolated and protected data processing environment under the control of the prospective provider and only authorised persons have access to those data
Note: Data environment control. Related conditions: (e) sharing only per Union data protection law, sandbox-created data not shared outside; (g) technical and organisational protection and deletion at end of participation or retention period.

If not met: [inference] the further processing is not permitted
Position: not stated
Quote: the logs of the processing of personal data in the context of the sandbox are kept for the duration of the participation in the sandbox
Note: Logging; 'unless provided otherwise by Union or national law'. Nearest named actor: the prospective provider.

Holder: Law enforcement authorities (processing under their control and responsibility)
Position: public authority: Member State authority
Quote: the processing of personal data in AI regulatory sandboxes shall be based on a specific Union or national law and subject to the same cumulative conditions as referred to in paragraph 1
Note: Applies to processing for prevention, investigation, detection or prosecution of criminal offences or execution of penalties. Art. 59(3) preserves other Union or national legal bases.

Level of obligation: statutory permission, subject to the conditions in Art. 60(4)
Holder: Providers or prospective providers of high-risk AI systems listed in Annex III
Position: outside the state: private companies (providers may also be public authorities)
Quote: Providers or prospective providers may conduct testing of high-risk AI systems referred to in Annex III in real world conditions at any time before the placing on the market or the putting into service of the AI system
Note: Testing. Trigger: before placing on the market or putting into service. Compared against: the real-world testing plan. Metric: not stated. May be done 'on their own or in partnership with one or more deployers or prospective deployers'; without prejudice to Art. 5 prohibitions and to any ethical review required by law (Art. 60(3)).

Statutory: non-statutory: EDPB Opinion 28/2024 (Art. 64(2) GDPR), interpreting GDPR Recital 26

Quote: If it can be demonstrated that the subsequent operation of the AI model does not entail the processing of personal data, the EDPB considers that the GDPR would not apply
Note: Scope decision (scenario 3: unlawful development, then anonymisation): the unlawfulness of the initial processing 'should not, therefore, impact the subsequent operation of the model'; personal data processed in deployment after anonymisation remains subject to the GDPR, and its lawfulness is not affected by the initial unlawfulness (para 135). But 'a mere assertion of anonymity of the model is not enough to exempt it from the application of the GDPR'; SAs assess anonymity on the Question 1 criteria and remain competent to intervene on the development-phase processing (para 133). Advisory: see note on the para 43 entry.

Note: Recall of the GDPR: the controller decides which legal basis it relies on for development and deployment processing. Statutory: non-statutory: WP29 Opinion 05/2014 on Anonymisation Techniques (referred to in EDPB Opinion 28/2024)
Holder: Article 29 Working Party (provider); competent SAs (to consider it)
Position: public authority: EU body (Article 29 Working Party, predecessor of the EDPB)

Note: Guidance resource serving the SA anonymity decision (Decision-making/Design, para 38). Per the Opinion, WP29 Opinion 05/2014 treats data as anonymous if it is not possible to single out, link and infer, and otherwise requires a thorough evaluation of identification risks; the EDPB considers AI models 'very likely to require such a thorough evaluation'. SAs should also consider 'the most recent WP29 opinions and/ or EDPB guidelines on the matter'. Official offer (prior EU-level guidance).

Statutory: non-statutory: EDPB Opinion 28/2024, interpreting GDPR Recital 26 and Art. 5(2)
Level of obligation: non-binding interpretation; non-prescriptive, non-exhaustive list (para 47); verb 'should' (addressed to SAs)
If not met: not stated here; see Accountability/Design entry (paras 45, 57)
Position: not specified: controllers may be public authorities or outside the state (e.g. private companies); the Opinion does not distinguish
Quote: SAs should evaluate the approach es taken by controllers during the development phase. The application and effectiveness of four key areas (identified below) should be considered in this regard.
Note: Framed as what SAs should evaluate; the measures are the controller's [inference that controllers are expected to take them]. Four areas: selection of sources (criteria, relevance, exclusion of inappropriate sources, para 50); data preparation and minimisation (anonymous or pseudonymised data considered, reasons if not, minimisation, filtering, para 51); methodological choices (regularisation to reduce overfitting and, 'crucially', privacy-preserving techniques e.g. differential privacy, para 52); measures on model outputs lowering the likelihood of obtaining training personal data via queries (para 53). Trigger: development phase. 'The presence or absence of the elements listed below is not a conclusive criterion' (para 48).

Statutory: non-statutory: EDPB Opinion 28/2024, interpreting GDPR Recital 26
Position: not specified: controllers may be public authorities or outside the state (e.g. private companies); the Opinion does not distinguish
Quote: SAs should consider whether controllers have assessed the risk of identification by the controller and by different types of ‘ other persons’, including unintended third parties accessing the AI model
Note: Risk assessment by the controller, considering whether others can reasonably gain access. Means assessed on objective factors (para 41): characteristics of training data, model and training procedure; release context; additional information available; cost and time; available technology. Also 'unintended (re)use or disclosure of the model' (para 43). Trigger: not stated.

Statutory: statutory: GDPR Arts 5, 24, 25, 30 and, where likely high risk, Art. 35
Level of obligation: statutory duty (EDPB interprets it as covering AI model training, including where the aim is anonymisation)
If not met: if the SA cannot confirm 'that effective measures were taken to anonymise the AI model, the SA would be in a position to consider that the controller has failed to meet  its accountability obligations under Art icle 5(2) GDPR' (para 57)
Position: not specified: controllers may be public authorities or outside the state (e.g. private companies); the Opinion does not distinguish
Quote: require controllers to adequately document their processing  operations. This also applies to any processing that would include the training of an AI model
Note: Recording. Continues 'even if the objective of the processing is  anonymisation'. Para 58 lists what the documentation 'ideally' includes: DPIA information (including decisions that no DPIA was needed); DPO advice; technical and organisational measures with threat model and risk assessments, per-source measures including source URLs; lifecycle measures; documentation of resistance to re-identification (training-data/parameter ratio, re-identification metrics, test reports and results); documentation provided to deployers and data subjects. Also coded Accountability/Design (paras 45, 57).

Statutory: non-statutory: EDPB Opinion 28/2024, interpreting GDPR Art. 6(1)(f)
Position: not specified
Quote: SAs may consider whether measures have been implemented to avoid a potential misuse of the AI  model.
Note: Passive. Nearest named actors: the controller whose measures are assessed, and SAs. For models deployable for many purposes 'such as generative AI', controls 'limiting as much as possible their use for harmful practices', e.g. creation of deepfakes, chatbots used for disinformation, phishing and fraud, manipulative AI/AI agents. Part of assessing the likelihood of further consequences in the balancing test. Trigger: not stated.

Statutory: non-statutory: EDPB Opinion 28/2024 (examples of mitigating measures)
Position: not specified: controllers may be public authorities or outside the state (e.g. private companies); the Opinion does not distinguish
Quote: Excluding collection from websites (or sections of websites) which clearly object to web scraping and the reuse of their content  for the purpose of building AI training databases
Note: Other examples: excluding content that might include personal data entailing risks for particular persons or groups; excluding certain data categories or sources, e.g. particularly intrusive websites; respecting robots.txt or ai.txt; other limits on collection, e.g. time periods. Holder from para 104 ('controllers conducting web scraping'). Trigger: development phase, at collection. Opt-out list (para 106) noted under Accountability/Design.

Statutory: non-statutory: EDPB Opinion 28/2024 (examples of mitigating measures)
Level of obligation: optional ('may'); 'should be assessed by SAs on a case-by-case basis'
Position: not specified
Quote: Technical measures may for instance be put in place to prevent the storage, regurgitation or generation of personal data, especially in the context of generative AI models (such as output filters)
Note: Passive. Nearest named actor: the controller deploying the model. Also measures to mitigate unlawful reuse by general-purpose AI models, 'e.g. digital watermarking of AI-generated outputs' (para 107(a)); measures beyond legal requirements facilitating rights in deployment, e.g. erasure from model output data, deduplication, post-training techniques to remove or suppress personal data (para 107(b)). Trigger: deployment phase. Bears on checking AI outputs.

Statutory: statutory: GDPR Arts 5(1)(a), 5(2), 6 and 24, as interpreted in EDPB Opinion 28/2024
If not met: not stated; the SA takes the assessment into account (para 129)
Holder: Controller deploying the model (acquired from another controller)
Position: not specified: controllers may be public authorities or outside the state (e.g. private companies); the Opinion does not distinguish
Quote: The controller should consider, for instance, if the data originates from a personal data breach or if the processing was subject to the finding of an infringement from a SA  or a court
Note: Pre-use check by the deployer of a model developed by another controller (scenario 2): ascertain 'that the AI model was not developed by unlawfully processing personal data' (para 129). Compared against: source of the data, personal data breaches, infringement findings by an SA or court. Depth of assessment and SAs' expected detail vary with the risks of the processing in deployment for the data subjects whose data trained the model. Trigger: not stated [inference: before or at deployment]. Directly relevant where a public body acquires a third-party model [inference]. Also coded Accountability/Design (para 129) and Delivery/Resources (documentation from developer, para 58(f)).

Statutory: non-statutory: EDPB Opinion 28/2024, interpreting GDPR Art. 6(1)(f)
Position: not specified
Quote: when the subsequent processing is based on legitimate interest,  the fact that the initial processing was unlawful should be taken into account in the legitimate interest assessment
Note: Passive. Nearest named actors: the controller assessing legitimate interest for subsequent (e.g. deployment) processing; SAs verify (para 132). Applies in scenario 1 (same controller) and scenario 2 (another controller), where technical aspects (filters or access limits the subsequent controller cannot circumvent) and legal aspects (nature and severity of the unlawfulness) 'have to be given due consideration within the balancing test' (para 132). Trigger: when subsequent processing relies on legitimate interest.

Level of obligation: statutory duty where processing is likely to result in high risk (recalled; not analysed in the Opinion)
Position: not specified
Quote: DPIAs are an important element of accountability, where the processing in the context of AI models is likely to result in a high risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons
Note: Impact assessment. Passive; nearest actor: controllers (Art. 35, not quoted). Listed among provisions 'This Opinion does not analyse' but which may still play an important role. The document calls DPIAs 'an important element of accountability'; coded Delivery as an impact assessment per the coding frame. Trigger: likely high risk; timing not stated. Points to WP29 DPIA Guidelines (fn 15). Para 58(a): SAs should ideally check DPIA information, including decisions that a DPIA was not necessary.

Level of obligation: statutory duty (recalled; not analysed in the Opinion)
Position: not specified

Note: Passive for the duty-holder; nearest actor: controllers (Art. 25(1), not quoted). SAs are named as assessors, so this could also be read as Accountability. Listed among provisions not analysed by the Opinion.

Statutory: statutory: GDPR Art. 5(1)(b) and (c), as interpreted in EDPB Opinion 28/2024
Position: not specified
Quote: the development and deployment  of AI models requires that personal data should be adequate, relevant and necessary in relation to the purpose.
Note: Passive; nearest actor: controllers. Continues: 'This can include the processing of personal data to avoid the risks of potential biases and errors when this is clearly and specifically identified within the purpose, and the personal data is necessary for that purpose' (bias and error checking). The purpose of development should be informed by the deployment context (para 64). Trigger: development and deployment.

Statutory: non-statutory: EDPB Opinion 28/2024, interpreting GDPR Arts 5(2), 24 and 30

Note: Information provided by the developer that serves the deployer's due-diligence check (Delivery/Design, para 130). Framed as content of the developer's documentation that SAs ideally verify. Also coded Coordination/Design (same passage).

Statutory: non-statutory: EDPB Guidelines 1/2024 on Art. 6(1)(f) GDPR (referred to in EDPB Opinion 28/2024)

Note: Guidance serving the legitimate interest assessment and balancing test (Delivery/Design entries, paras 66, 77). The Opinion builds 'on the Guidelines 1/2024' (para 59) and cites them throughout (fns 39-82). Official offer.

Statutory: statutory: GDPR Art. 6(1)(f) and Art. 5(2), as interpreted in EDPB Opinion 28/2024

Position: not specified: controllers may be public authorities or outside the state (e.g. private companies); the Opinion does not distinguish

Position: not specified: controllers may be public authorities or outside the state (e.g. private companies); the Opinion does not distinguish

Statutory: non-statutory: EDPB Opinion 28/2024 (mitigating measures beyond the GDPR)
Level of obligation: optional ('may'); additional safeguard beyond Art. 21 GDPR

Note: Measures that facilitate individuals' rights (para 102): a reasonable period between collecting a training dataset and using it; unconditional opt-out before processing; erasure even where Art. 17(1) grounds do not apply. Holder from para 96 ('the controller may consider introducing mitigating measures'). To whom: data subjects.

Statutory: non-statutory: EDPB Opinion 28/2024 (mitigating measures beyond the GDPR)
Level of obligation: optional ('could include'); voluntary transparency beyond GDPR obligations
Position: not specified: controllers may be public authorities or outside the state (e.g. private companies); the Opinion does not distinguish
Quote: Release of public and easily accessible communications which go beyond the information required under Article 13 or 14 GDPR, for instance by providing additional details  about the collection criteria and all datasets used
Note: Publication. Optional transparency measures to reduce information asymmetry about development: public communications beyond Arts 13-14 (collection criteria, datasets); media and e-mail campaigns, graphic visualisation, FAQs, 'transparency labels  and model cards', and 'annual transparency reports on a voluntary basis' (para 103(b)). To whom: data subjects and the public. Holder from para 96.

Statutory: statutory: GDPR Art. 5(1)(a) read with Art. 5(2), as interpreted in EDPB Opinion 28/2024

If not met: not stated; SA corrective powers (paras 113-115) apply to the initial processing (para 127)

Position: not specified: controllers may be public authorities or outside the state (e.g. private companies); the Opinion does not distinguish

Note: Preceded by 'each controller should ensure the lawfulness of the processing it conducts and be able to demonstrate it'. To whom: competent SAs. Statutory: statutory: GDPR Art. 58(2), as interpreted in EDPB Opinion 28/2024
If not met: 'issuing a fine, imposing a temporary limitation on the processing, erasing part of the dataset that was processed unlawfully' or ordering erasure of the whole dataset and/or the AI model itself (para 114)
Position: not specified: controllers may be public authorities or outside the state (e.g. private companies); the Opinion does not distinguish

Level of obligation: statutory duty (pointer; not analysed in the Opinion)

Note: Pointer only: the Opinion does not analyse Art. 22. Coded Accountability because the safeguards concern challenge of automated decisions [inference; the Opinion does not list them]. Statutory: non-statutory: Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content, Section 1 (voluntary; implementing AI Act Art. 50(2) and (5))
Position: n/a
Quote: This Section of the Code applies to Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems falling within Article 2 and Article 50(2) AI Act
Note: Sets who is bound (scope and exemptions). Holder not stated: the scope is set by the Code itself; the cover names the Working Group 1 chair and vice-chairs. Value chain: 'providers of generative AI models that are placed on the Union market independently from AI systems and third -party providers of marking and detection solutions may also, on a voluntary basis, adhere'. Recital (g): 'simplified ways of compliance for SMEs and SMCs, including startups, should be possible'. Exemptions inside measures: a single marking layer suffices for products in a closed environment and for free-form text (Measure 1.1); no watermark needed for 'very short text' under 200 tokens (Sub-measure 1.1.2, Glossary).

Statutory: non-statutory: Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content, Section 1 (voluntary; implementing AI Act Art. 50(2) and (5))
Level of obligation: mandatory under the Code for Signatories ('will'); adherence to the Code is voluntary
If not met: not stated (compliance monitored by competent market surveillance authorities; no consequence stated)
Holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
Position: outside the state: private companies (mainly); a public body providing a generative AI system would also be covered [inference]
Quote: Signatories will record information in the metadata on whether the content is AI-generated or manipulated. All recorded information will be digitally signed and time -stamped
Note: Recording in metadata where the format supports it (audio, image, video, containerised text). Signing certificates and private keys to be secured, except where the deployment context does not allow, e.g. local deployment. Richer metadata encouraged (Measure 1.3: system name, provider name, timestamp; may add model identifier and version) without privacy- or business-sensitive information.

Statutory: non-statutory: Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content, Section 1 (voluntary; implementing AI Act Art. 50(2) and (5))
Level of obligation: mandatory under the Code for Signatories ('will'); adherence to the Code is voluntary
If not met: not stated (compliance monitored by competent market surveillance authorities; no consequence stated)
Holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
Position: outside the state: private companies (mainly); a public body providing a generative AI system would also be covered [inference]
Quote: Signatories will ensure that AI -generated or manipulated content  is marked with an imperceptible watermark, with the exception of very short text.
Note: Exception: very short text, under 200 tokens (Glossary). Free-form text over 200 tokens must still be watermarked, though less reliably; access to its detection may be restricted to verified expert users. The watermark is to be 'difficult for it to be separated from the content' and complements the signed metadata. Model-level watermarking by model providers coded Delivery/Resources.

Statutory: non-statutory: Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content, Section 1 (voluntary)
Level of obligation: optional ('may'); safeguards are mandatory ('will') if the option is used
Holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
Position: outside the state: private companies (mainly); a public body providing a generative AI system would also be covered [inference]
Quote: Signatories may implement as an optional supplementary measure fingerprinting or logging solutions for AI -generated or manipulated
Note: Quote breaks at a page boundary; the text continues 'content which allow for checking whether content has been generated or manipulated by their AI system'. 'relying on fingerprinting or logging alone is not considered sufficient'. If implemented, Signatories 'will ensure that it is limited to the output data', privacy-preserving and respecting media freedom and journalistic source protection. It 'shall in no way be interpreted as creating a general commitment to log, monitor, or retain prompts'. Deployers' control over logging coded Decision-making/Design.

Statutory: non-statutory: Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content, Section 1 (voluntary)
Holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems (provide); deployers and other users (receive)
Position: outside the state: private companies (mainly); a public body providing a generative AI system would also be covered [inference]
Quote: Deployers and other users of the generative AI systems will be given access to the logging policies
Note: Information provided to deployers, serving their control over logging (Decision-making/Design, same passage). Only where the provider uses the optional logging.

Statutory: non-statutory: Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content, Section 1 (voluntary; implementing AI Act Art. 50(2))
Level of obligation: mandatory under the Code for Signatories ('will', 'best efforts'); adherence to the Code is voluntary
If not met: not stated (compliance monitored by competent market surveillance authorities; no consequence stated)
Holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
Position: outside the state: private companies (mainly); a public body providing a generative AI system would also be covered [inference]
Quote: Signatories will, to the extent technically feasible and recognisable as per open standards, retain, and abstain from intentionally altering or removing, existing metadata markings, where such content is used as input
Note: Exceptions: good-faith legitimate processing, e.g. security audits and research. Statutory: non-statutory: Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content, Section 1 (voluntary)
Level of obligation: optional ('may'); access for expert users is mandatory ('will')
Holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
Position: outside the state: private companies (mainly); a public body providing a generative AI system would also be covered [inference]
Quote: Signatories may restrict access to detection mechanisms associated to watermarking techniques for free-form text to the extent that they have a lower level of reliability and robustness
Note: Authority over who may use a detection tool, because such detection may give 'misleading or low -confidence results'. But Signatories 'will ensure that  access for these expert end-users is granted' (including competent MSAs, other regulators and law enforcement), and restrictions 'will be limited in time'. The same applies to optional forensic detection (Measure 2.2).

Statutory: non-statutory: Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content, Section 1 (voluntary; refers to EU data protection law)
Level of obligation: mandatory under the Code for Signatories ('will'); adherence to the Code is voluntary
If not met: not stated (compliance monitored by competent market surveillance authorities; no consequence stated)
Holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
Position: outside the state: private companies (mainly); a public body providing a generative AI system would also be covered [inference]
Quote: Signatories will ensure that the detection is compliant with EU privacy and data protection law.
Note: For detection that requires uploading content: treat content as privacy-sensitive; confidentiality and integrity in transit and at rest; data minimisation; sole purpose of detection; 'zero retention' (content deleted immediately after detection, no verbatim copy kept, minimal traffic logs for security only); security safeguards; third-country transfer rules; cybersecurity best practice. Bears on public bodies uploading content for checking [inference].

Statutory: non-statutory: Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content, Section 1 (voluntary)
Level of obligation: mandatory under the Code for Signatories ('will'); adherence to the Code is voluntary
If not met: not stated (compliance monitored by competent market surveillance authorities; no consequence stated)

Note: Quote breaks at a page boundary; continues 'to the competent market surveillance authorities, subject to confidentiality and security safeguards to enable them to detect , where necessary,  legacy content'. Statutory: non-statutory: Code of Practice on Transparency of AI-generated Content, Section 1 (voluntary)
Holder: Signatories who are providers of generative AI systems
Position: outside the state: private companies (mainly); a public body providing a generative AI system would also be covered [inference]
Quote: Signatories may include as part of their detection solution, as an additional optional measure, forensic detection mechanism to detect content generated or manipulated by their AI system or underlying model for which marking has been stripped.
Note: If used: privacy and security as in Sub-measure 2.1.3, clear disclosure (Measure 2.3), best efforts to match the state of the art.
